blocks.orig: The Maasai tribe is one of the most prominent tribes in Kenya and northern Tanzania. The Maasai people ethnically belong to the Nilotic group and have an incredibly rich culture, from their distinct attire to their distinctive Maa language and traditions. Though Maa is the official language of the Masaai, most Maasai people also speak the official languages of Tanzania and Kenya: Swahili and English!
blocks.html: In Kenya and northern Tanzania, the Maasai are one of the best-known tribes. Ethnically they belong to the Nilotic group, and their culture is remarkably rich, from their distinctive clothing to their own Maa language and customs. Although Maa is the official Maasai tongue, most Maasai also speak Swahili and English, the official languages of Tanzania and Kenya.

blocks.orig: The piercing and stretching of the earlobes is a common practice among the Maasai, with women often wearing colourful beaded ornaments in their ears.
blocks.html: Piercing and stretching the earlobes is widespread among the Maasai, and women frequently wear brightly coloured beaded ornaments in their ears.

blocks.orig: Many Tanzania tourists are looking for a deeper experience to their safari adventure, and wish to visit a Maasai village during their trip to Tanzania. These visits occur during or in between safaris, as the Maasai tribe live close to the national parks – think of lush natural destinations like the vast Serengeti or the Ngorongoro Crater.

blocks.orig: The Maasai love to share their incredible culture with visitors. So when visiting a Maasai tribe, you can expect to see several Maasai traditions first hand. This includes celebratory dances and songs and a closer look at the beautiful jewellery made with typical Maasai beads.
blocks.html: The Maasai take real pleasure in sharing their remarkable culture with guests, so during a visit you can expect to witness several traditions first hand. Among them are celebratory songs and dances, and a close look at the lovely jewellery crafted from typical Maasai beads.

blocks.html: Things to know before visiting a Maasai tribe

blocks.orig: Various Maasai villages host many tours to international travellers every day. This means you should be aware that you may not be the only tourist in the village! Visiting a Maasai village has become a significant part of promoting Maasai culture for many villages in Tanzania. This not only shares the beauty of the ancient Maasai culture, but creates an additional source of income for the tribe.
blocks.html: Several Maasai villages welcome many groups of international travellers each day, so bear in mind that you may well not be the only tourist there. For numerous villages in Tanzania, hosting visitors has become an important way of promoting Maasai culture. It shares the beauty of this ancient culture and, at the same time, gives the tribe an extra source of income.

blocks.orig: Do ask questions! Your Maasai hosts are there to share their culture and welcome questions about their culture and traditions.
blocks.html: Do ask questions. Your Maasai hosts are there to share their way of life and are happy to answer questions about their culture and traditions.

blocks.orig: Don’t take photos without permission! Always ask for permission when taking photos of the Maasai village and the Maasai people.
blocks.html: Don’t photograph anyone without asking. Always request permission before taking pictures of the Maasai village or the Maasai people.

blocks.orig: Do respect your environment. It’s important to remember that this is not a tourist attraction – it is the home of your hosts.
blocks.html: Do treat your surroundings with respect. It’s worth remembering that this is not a tourist attraction – you are in the home of your hosts.

blocks.orig: Do purchase souvenirs. The Maasai’s selection of handcrafted souvenirs are fantastic gifts and keepsakes to remind you of your time in Tanzania.
